title: When AI Meets the Web: Prompt Injection Risks in Third-Party AI Chatbot Plugins
reason: Prompt injection is the central phenomenon, with large-scale empirical analysis of direct and indirect injection risks in web chatbot plugins. The study evaluates concrete vulnerabilities, attack amplification, untrusted external content, and model/system-prompt factors across real deployments.

title: Hijacking Large Audio-Language Models via Context-Agnostic and Imperceptible Auditory Prompt Injection
reason: The work directly introduces and evaluates auditory prompt injection for large audio-language models. It provides a concrete attack framework, mechanisms for stealth and context generalization, extensive multi-model experiments, success rates, and real-world voice-agent demonstrations.

title: SoK: Robustness in Large Language Models against Jailbreak Attacks
reason: Jailbreak attacks and defenses are the explicit focus. The paper offers a systematic taxonomy, a multidimensional evaluation framework, comparative synthesis, and benchmark studies covering representative attacks and defenses.

title: Parasites in the Toolchain: A Large-Scale Analysis of Attacks on the MCP Ecosystem
reason: The main contribution is a malicious-instruction attack on MCP toolchains in which adversarial instructions are embedded in external data and propagate into sensitive tool calls. Although distinguished from traditional prompt injection, it is directly relevant to indirect instruction manipulation and is supported by a large-scale ecosystem analysis.

title: AttnTrace: Contextual Attribution of Prompt Injection and Knowledge Corruption
reason: Prompt injection is a major focus alongside knowledge corruption, with a method for tracing malicious context and improving injection detection. The study is especially relevant to RAG and agents using retrieved or Internet content and reports systematic comparative evaluation.

title: Lineage: A UMA2.0 Protocol Extension for Multi-Hop LLM Agent Delegation
reason: The study primarily addresses authorization and delegation security for LLM agents rather than prompt injection itself. It remains relevant because the protocol is experimentally tested against an active prompt-injection attempt and blocks it at the authorization layer independently of model behavior.

title: Sentinel-Math: A Framework for Neural Intent Monitoring and SafetyCircuit-Breaking Against Semantically Disguised Logical Tasks in LLMs
reason: The paper proposes a defense against semantically disguised harmful requests and reports jailbreak success rates on dedicated benchmarks. Its attack setting is relatively specialized around mathematical/logical tasks, but the defense, intent monitoring, and empirical jailbreak evaluation are relevant to the broader review.

title: PolyJailbreak: Cross-Modal Jailbreaking Attacks on Closed-Box Multimodal LLMs
reason: Jailbreaking is the central topic, with a new closed-box cross-modal attack framework and analysis of the underlying multimodal safety asymmetry. Extensive experiments across multiple MLLMs and commercial models provide clear attack-success evidence and comparison with baselines.

title: Ellipsoid Control: A White-List Jailbreak Defense via Benign Latent Modeling
reason: The study is explicitly centered on jailbreak defense and proposes a test-time white-list method based on benign latent modeling. It evaluates the defense across multiple LLMs, jailbreak attacks, benign tasks, and safety-boundary settings, directly informing defense effectiveness and utility trade-offs.

title: A Multi-Agent Framework for Step-Level Tool-Call Safety Evaluation in Industrial Control Systems
reason: Contextual prompt injection is a major evaluated threat within a benchmark for LLM-agent tool-call safety. The paper contributes a taxonomy, dataset, multi-domain benchmark, and guardrail evaluation showing difficulty detecting injection-induced unsafe behavior.

title: An Edge–Cloud Collaborative Framework for Latency Optimization in Prompt Injection Defense
reason: Prompt-injection defense is the explicit setting, but the main contribution optimizes routing and latency around an existing detection pipeline rather than introducing a new detector. Simulation results provide useful evidence about deployment trade-offs for risk-stratified prompt-injection checking.

title: Trust-Aware Orchestration Architecture for LLM-Assisted Workflows in Multi-Tenant Enterprise Systems
reason: Prompt injection is one of several enterprise LLM risks, but the architecture directly evaluates injection benchmarks, sanitization, deterministic enforcement gates, and adaptive attacks. The substantial multi-model evaluation and agent/RAG context make it useful for understanding practical defenses and their limitations.

title: Securing in-Vehicle Large Language Models: A Taxonomy of Integration, Threats, and Trustworthiness
reason: Prompt injection appears as one threat within a broader taxonomy of in-vehicle LLM security, alongside hallucination, adversarial manipulation, and data leakage. The structured threat analysis and design guidelines are potentially useful, but the application is specialized and prompt injection is not the central phenomenon.

title: Study the Effectiveness of Existing Detection Mechanisms Against Prompt Injection in LLMs
reason: The article is directly focused on prompt-injection detection and uses a systematic review approach to compare mechanisms by metrics, threat models, latency, and deployment constraints. Its categorization of detection approaches and synthesis of trade-offs directly support several review questions.

title: Enterprise Search Portals: Hybrid RAG at Scale for Compliance-Sensitive Knowledge Work
reason: The main focus is a policy-first enterprise RAG architecture, while prompt injection and retriever poisoning are secondary threats addressed through security controls. Its strong RAG context and evaluated architecture are relevant, but the abstract does not indicate a dedicated experimental evaluation of prompt-injection attacks or defenses.

title: External Data Extraction Attacks Against Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
reason: The central threat is external data extraction from RAG systems rather than prompt injection itself, but the attack framework explicitly incorporates jailbreak operators and optimized jailbreak prompts. It provides a formal attack model, concrete mechanisms, multi-model experiments, defense evaluation, and a highly relevant RAG setting.

title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Transformer Framework for Detecting Adversarial Prompts in Healthcare Chatbots
reason: Prompt-injection detection is the explicit focus, using federated learning to train a privacy-preserving classifier for healthcare chatbots. The abstract reports a named dataset, multiple training settings, and detailed accuracy, precision, recall, F1, and AUC results.

title: Research on Security Enhancement Methods for Adversarial Robust Large Language Model Intelligent Agents for Medical Decision-Making Tasks
reason: Prompt injection is one of several adversarial threats evaluated against a security framework for medical LLM agents. The work provides attack-success results, baseline comparisons, and ablations, offering useful defense evidence despite its broader multi-threat and domain-specific focus.

title: ShadowCode: Toward (Automatic) External Prompt Injection Attack Against Code LLMs
reason: The study directly proposes an automatic external prompt-injection attack against Code LLMs using malicious perturbations embedded in code context, dependencies, or RAG knowledge bases. It evaluates multiple objectives, languages, open-source models, and commercial applications with explicit attack-success rates.

title: Intelligent Multi-Agent Reinforcement Sanitizer for Securing LLM Systems
reason: The paper centers on defending LLMs against prompt poisoning/prompt injection and proposes a multi-agent pipeline combining detection, sanitization, integrity checking, temporal analysis, and multimodal inspection. Experimental validation is stated across multiple attack conditions, although the abstract provides fewer quantitative details than the strongest empirical studies.
